plain: To take away from or reduce the force of something.

webster.text: To repeal, annul or destroy the force and effect of some part of a law or established rule; to lessen the extent of a law; distinguished from abrogate.

example.quote: and we shall never find two thirds of a Congress voting or proposing any thing which shall derogate from their own authority and importance, or agreeing to give back to the people any part of those privileges which they have once parted with–so far from it;
example.cite: An Old Whig I, Philadelphia Independent Gazetteer, Oct. 12, 1787
